subject: Feasibility check: Combined HIPAA/GLBA addendum for CardioHealth integration
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@cardiohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: Can Redwood support a combined HIPAA + GLBA addendum for our pilot?

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this—CardioHealth is evaluating Redwood for a small pilot that spans two regulated domains: patient data (HIPAA) and certain consumer financial data elements (GLBA) because we provide patient financing in partnership with a regional credit union. Our legal & security teams would like to understand whether Redwood can: 

- Execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) while simultaneously honoring GLBA contractual constraints (we have a GLBA addendum template we can share).
- Limit subprocessor residency to US regions and provide a list of committed subprocessors, with options for Dedicated capacity if needed.
- Provide encrypted backups, key rotation controls (KMS), and export controls documentation.

I've attached a short integration scope and a draft SOW that outline the planned data flows and a list of required assurances. Can you confirm feasibility and next steps? Ideally we'd have a technical + legal sync this week.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Integrations, CardioHealth
attachments: integration_scope.pdf, CardioHealth_SOW_draft.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@cardiohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support a combined HIPAA + GLBA addendum for our pilot?

Hi Maria,

Appreciate the detail—this is a great brief. I'm looping in Ben (security/infra) and Laura (privacy/contracts) so we can assess the ask across legal and operational controls. High-level response: we typically support BAAs and have pathways for GLBA addenda, but combined constraints (especially residency + limited subprocessors + financial-data controls) usually push us toward Dedicated or Private deployment for predictable isolation and contractual commitments.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben / Laura: can you review the attached scope and the two explicit asks (BAA + GLBA addendum compatibility + residency limits) and flag any blockers or required redlines?
- Maria: would you be available for a 45-minute joint call Wednesday 6/9 at 10am PT to walk through the SOW and acceptance criteria?

I can produce a short addenda outline after we align internally.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0178
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support a combined HIPAA + GLBA addendum for our pilot?

Naomi, Maria,

Thanks for the summary. Quick operational notes from infra/security perspective: 

- Residency & subprocessors: We can limit primary processing to US regions and provide a committed subprocessors list, but full elimination of all third-party cloud services is only feasible with Dedicated or Private deployments. For Hosted (multi-tenant) we operate with a broader subprocessor set and cannot commit to an exhaustive, immutable list.
- Dedicated: offers tenant isolation + control plane options for VPC peering. That path also supports in-scope SOC2 controls and attestation for encryption in transit/at rest.
- KV cache & logs: We can implement strict retention windows and encryption keys (KMS) scoped per-customer in Dedicated. However, GLBA requires stronger controls around payment-data handling; we need to know if CardioHealth wants Redwood to process raw financial identifiers or if tokenized references will be used.
- Attachments: I started a security questionnaire skeleton (security_questionnaire.xlsx) that we can send to CardioHealth to collect specifics (encryption algorithms, audit log retention window, expected TPS, model-level PII filtering requirements).

Open questions for the technical call: expected QPS, sequence lengths, whether they require enclave-level attestations, and an initial list of fields that will be considered GLBA-sensitive.

Ben Carter
Head of Security & Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@cardiohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support a combined HIPAA + GLBA addendum for our pilot?

Team, Maria,

From a contracts/privacy lens, there are a few key considerations: 

- Contract structure: We typically separate the BAA (HIPAA obligations) from any GLBA addendum language, but we can provide a combined exhibit that covers both sets of obligations to reduce signature clutter. We'll need CardioHealth's GLBA template to map required clauses (data classification, permitted use, audit rights).
- Subprocessors: We can provide a committed list and add a 30–60 day notice for changes. For strict residency + restricted subprocessors we should recommend Dedicated + a tailored subprocessor clause that includes approval rights for a short initial list.
- Liability & indemnity: GLBA may require different liability carve-outs around data misuse; we'll need risk acceptance from Redwood leadership for any expanded indemnity — this is typically reviewed at the Director level.
- Evidence: CardioHealth will request SOC2 reports, encryption attestations, and possibly penetration-test summaries. We can provide redacted reports and our SOC2 Type II (scope permitting).

If product can confirm Dedicated feasibility (Ben), legal can draft a combined addenda outline that mirrors CardioHealth's template and highlights areas where we may need alternative mitigations.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal & Privacy, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@cardiohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support a combined HIPAA + GLBA addendum for our pilot?

Hi Maria—great call today, thanks everyone for joining. Summary and next steps: 

1) Feasibility (prelim): Redwood can support the combined requirements, but the most straightforward and contractually clean path is Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with US-only residency and a scoped subprocessor list. Hosted could be considered only if CardioHealth accepts a standard subprocessor notice and broader residency flexibility.

2) Action items: 
- CardioHealth: Please share the GLBA addendum template and a short list of fields you consider GLBA-sensitive before EOD Tuesday.
- Redwood (Ben): Complete the security questionnaire and confirm Dedicated-sizing estimates by Friday. Attachment: security_questionnaire.xlsx (in progress).
- Redwood (Laura): Draft a combined addenda outline (BAA + GLBA clauses) and circulate for redlines. Attachment: redwood_addenda_outline.pdf

3) Evidence: We'll share SOC2 Type II redacted and KMS export policy docs ahead of the legal review.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for next Wednesday 6/9 at 10am PT unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
